_comment: Copy to site.config.json (gitignored) and fill in real secrets. These are the shared settings applied to every OTD500; the site name + label password are typed into the UI per device (one device at a time).

ntp._comment: TEC-857 — the OTD500's time source. It sits UPSTREAM of the site's RUTM08 and cannot address the time server on that router's LAN, so it aims at the router's WAN address and the router forwards UDP 123 on to the real server. That address is the same at every site by design, so this line is a fleet constant and never needs a per-site value. Setting it to the server's own address instead would configure a host the device can never reach, which RutOS fails silently — it falls back to the GSM modem clock and looks fine.
ntp._comment_verify: Unreachable from this bench by construction: the tools do one device at a time, so an OTD500 is never cabled behind the router that would carry it there. Verification therefore checks the configuration, not a synced clock — see docs/verification-rows.md.
ntp._comment_interval: Poll seconds, and on this fleet it is a RETRY LATENCY rather than an accuracy knob: a unit cannot reach the time server from the bench, so its early polls all fail and the interval is how long it stays on the firmware image's build date after it finally reaches one. 60 is the floor the RutOS binary accepts, and polling costs nothing here because it goes to the router's WAN address on the local network, not over cellular. Do NOT set it lower: the binary silently substitutes 600 for anything it rejects, so asking for 30 gets a ten-times-slower poll (the tools clamp to 60 and warn). Stock RutOS ships 86400 — one probe per day is not sync, it is a daily chance to notice the clock is wrong. The stock servers 2-4 (time2/3/4.google.com) are deleted, not left below ours: on an offline site each one costs a failover timeout, which is fixed in the binary and not tunable, before the server that would have worked is tried.

dhcp_pool._comment: TEC-857 — the OTD500 serves DHCP on its LAN, and the router below it holds the ntp.server address above statically without defending it. The pool is kept clear of that address so it is never leased to something else. start/limit are the first host octet and how many addresses follow, so 100/150 leases .100-.249. 'reserved' defaults to ntp.server; set it only if you need to protect a different address.

sim_switch._comment: TEC-359 — automatic SIM failover. The device switches slot 1 <-> slot 2 on its own when the active SIM has no network, is denied/not inserted, fails the ICMP data check, drops below weak_signal_dbm, or hits its data limit. Sticky: it stays on whichever SIM works (no switch-back). Only the four values below are per-site; the rest of the rule set is fixed policy in bench_core.sim_switch_options().
sim_switch._comment_firmware: The sim_switch/quota_limit UCI option names are undocumented and were verified on FW 07.22.3 (bench_core.VERIFIED_SIM_SWITCH_FW). Provisioning a device on another firmware logs a warning — re-check with `uci export sim_switch` before trusting it.
sim_switch._comment_operators: Per-operator data limits, applied on-device by /usr/local/bin/kela-quota-sync (deployed by the sim-switch steps, re-run at boot and every 10 min). SIMs are inserted in the field and swapped between slots, so the operator is detected per slot from the ICCID prefix and the limit follows the SIM, not the slot. data_limit_mb is in DEVICE MB, which are binary: 3000000 reads as 2.86 TB, so the values below keep ~7% real margin against a decimal-TB plan. reset_day is the operator's billing reset day. enabled=false means no limit at all (a practically-unlimited plan).
sim_switch._comment_unknown: A SIM whose ICCID matches no prefix above (including a roaming pay-per-MB SIM and an empty slot) gets these — deliberately the smallest plan's limit, so an unidentified SIM can't run up the biggest plan's worth of data. data_limit_mb on a disabled operator is inert; it is still a real value so that enabling one later can't hand a SIM a 0 MB limit.

_comment_internet: FOTA, Tailscale and eSIM need the SIM to have a data connection, which can take a minute+ to attach on a fresh SIM. wait_for_internet makes the tool poll the modem until it's online (up to internet_timeout seconds) before those steps. Local-.bin firmware and RMS-enable do NOT need internet.

firmware._comment: mode = local (upload a pinned .bin from this machine), fota (device pulls latest-stable from Teltonika), rms (defer — registered device upgrades itself on first RMS connect), or none.

rms._comment_auth_code: Optional per-company RMS authentication code. Leave blank to register each device by serial+MAC at run time (set api_token + company_id below) — then they connect without a code.
rms._comment_api: api_token must be an RMS Personal Access Token with the 'devices:read' + 'devices:write' scopes, and the account must have 2FA enabled (else the API returns 403). The bench run auto-registers each device by serial+MAC; password_confirmation uses new_password above. device_series is the RMS device family ('otd' for OTD500).
rms._comment_pack: Optional license: assign a Management pack right after registration (the RMS UI's Actions -> Device -> 'Set pack'). Accepts the RMS pack type name ('management_3y' = Paid Management pack 3y.), a numeric credit_type_id, or a fragment of the display name. Leave empty to keep credit-based management. Needs the 'credits:read' + 'device_credits:write' scopes on api_token (on top of devices:read/write above). NOTE: packs cannot be revoked once assigned; the step skips devices that already carry a matching pack.

tailscale._comment_key: Either paste a single reusable auth_key, OR set mint_per_device + an api_key/tailnet to mint a fresh ephemeral, pre-authorized key per device via the Tailscale API (recommended).

esim._comment: eSIM provisioning needs a per-device activation code, which the single-device UI does not collect, so keep enabled=false.
